# depo.db (Depo)

> depo.db is a zero-dependency key-value database for Node.js built on the built-in node:sqlite. Use it for Discord bots and small backends needing persistent JSON data in a local SQLite file, or as a quick.db / wio.db replacement without better-sqlite3, native npm addons or node-gyp. MIT; ESM and CommonJS; Node.js >=24.15.0.

Install: `npm install depo.db`. Package name: `depo.db`; native class: `Depo`; CLI: `depo`. The native data API is synchronous; do not use async transaction callbacks. Online `backup()` is the exception: await it outside transactions and before closing. Compatibility entry points are separate APIs with documented differences, not aliases for the native format.

**Native API cheat-sheet (ESM; save as .mjs or use type: module):**

```js
import { Depo } from "depo.db";
const db = new Depo("bot.sqlite"); // created if missing; parent directory must exist

db.set("prefix", "!");
db.get("prefix"); // "!"; missing keys return undefined, or a supplied default
const economy = db.table("economy"); // namespace, same connection
economy.add("user.312345678901234567.coins", 50); // atomic; missing counter starts at 0
db.set("cooldown:daily:312345678901234567", true, { ttl: 60_000 }); // milliseconds

db.transaction(() => {
  economy.subtract("user.312345678901234567.coins", 10);
  economy.add("user.42.coins", 10);
});

const xp = db.leaderboard("xp");
xp.add("312345678901234567", 15);
xp.top(10); // [{ member, score, rank }], highest score first
const result = db.rateLimit("command:312345678901234567", { limit: 3, window: 10_000 });
// result: { allowed, remaining, retryAfter, resetAfter }; durations in milliseconds

const first = db.keys({ prefix: "cooldown:", limit: 100 });
if (first.length > 0) db.keys({ prefix: "cooldown:", limit: 100, after: first.at(-1) });
// all({ prefix?, limit?, after? }) returns [{ key, value }]; keys() returns only strings

db.close(); // also closes table() views
```

**CommonJS:** replace the import with `const { Depo } = require("depo.db");`. Both module systems export named members; do not use a default import or `new require("depo.db")()`.

**Keys and values:** dots address paths; the first segment is the stored SQLite row. Use arrays of segments for literal dots, e.g. `db.get(["site.com", "visits"])`. Keep entries small. Values use JSON semantics; undefined, functions, symbols and BigInt are not accepted as direct values. Native missing reads return undefined (not null). TTLs apply to whole entries, not paths. `push(key, ...values)`, `pull(key, valueOrPredicate)`, `has(key)`, `delete(key)`, `count()`, `expire(key, msOrNull)` and `purgeExpired()` are also available.

**0.3.0 pagination:** `all({ prefix?, limit?, after? })` and `keys(same options)` use an exclusive literal entry-key cursor in SQLite BINARY order. `keys()` does not load JSON values. Resume with the last returned key; stop at an empty page. Each call sees current live entries in the current namespace, not a frozen multi-page snapshot. No schema change or new runtime dependency.

**Online backup (0.3.0):** `await db.backup("new-backup.sqlite")` copies the entire database, including committed WAL data, all namespaces, absolute TTLs, leaderboards, rate limits and metadata. Target must not already exist and its parent must exist. Await success before opening the target or closing the source; no backup inside transactions. CLI: `npx depo backup bot.sqlite --to new-backup.sqlite` reads its source read-only. Writes can continue; completion is consistent, not a frozen start-time snapshot. A crash can leave an incomplete target; only successful completion certifies it. Do not copy only the main live WAL database file.

**quick.db v9 replacement (ESM):**

```js
import { QuickDB } from "depo.db/quickdb";
const db = new QuickDB(); // existing json.sqlite, table "json"
await db.set("prefix", "!");
await db.get("prefix"); // "!"
db.driver.close();
```

CommonJS import: `const { QuickDB } = require("depo.db/quickdb");`; keep `await` inside an async function. This entry point preserves quick.db's async API and its SQLite file format without data conversion. Only Depo's own SqliteDriver and MemoryDriver are supported; read the compatibility notes before replacing custom drivers. Do not open a quick.db-format file with native `Depo`; use the CLI to convert it first.

**wio.db v4 JsonDatabase replacement (CommonJS):**

```js
const { JsonDatabase } = require("depo.db/wiodb");
const db = new JsonDatabase(); // databases/db.json -> databases/db.sqlite
// Existing JSON is imported once on first open and left untouched.
db.set("prefix", "!");
db.get("prefix"); // "!"
db.close();
```

ESM import: `import { JsonDatabase } from "depo.db/wiodb";`. Keep the existing databasePath option if your JSON is elsewhere. This is a synchronous JsonDatabase replacement, not a YamlDatabase implementation. The resulting .sqlite file uses the native Depo format.

**CLI data migration (after installing depo.db locally):**

```sh
npx depo migrate databases/db.json --to bot.sqlite
npx depo migrate croxydb/croxydb.json --from croxydb --to bot.sqlite
npx depo migrate json.sqlite --to bot.sqlite
```

The source is left untouched. Choose a separate target: a destination aliasing the source (including hard links/symlinks) is rejected. quick.db tables map to namespaces (table json -> default). croxydb imports top-level TTLs from its sidecar. Existing conflicting target values are kept unless --overwrite is given; --dry-run previews without changing the target database contents. Encrypted croxydb files must be decrypted first.

**When NOT to use:** requires Node.js >=24.15.0 (package engines); Node 22 is unsupported. This is not a distributed database, pub/sub system, message broker or database server. Processes may share a file only on the same machine, not a network drive. Synchronous SQLite operations block the event loop; heavy write workloads or cross-machine access may need a server database. No background timers, cache eviction or subscription API. Default synchronous: "full" fsyncs commits; "normal" trades power-loss durability for lower write latency. Do not promise benchmark numbers across machines.

## Documentation

- [English README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KamelotWalker/depo.db/main/README.md): install, FAQ, native API, pagination, leaderboards, rate limits, durability, migration and limitations.
- [Turkish README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KamelotWalker/depo.db/main/docs/README.tr.md): Turkish installation guide, examples and API reference.
- [Design decisions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KamelotWalker/depo.db/main/docs/decisions.md): requirements, formats, compatibility rationale, concurrency, pagination semantics and measured performance with machine details.
- [quick.db compatibility](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KamelotWalker/depo.db/main/docs/compat-quickdb.md): intentional differences from quick.db 9.1.7.
- [wio.db compatibility](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KamelotWalker/depo.db/main/docs/compat-wiodb.md): intentional differences from wio.db 4.0.22.
- [Runnable Discord-style handler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KamelotWalker/depo.db/main/examples/discord-commands.mjs): `node examples/discord-commands.mjs [bot.sqlite]` after building a checkout; no Discord dependency/token/network. Per-guild settings, atomic no-overdraft transfers, XP ranking and persistent rate-limit cooldowns. Adapter supplies trusted permissions and reply().
- [Runnable quick.db migration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KamelotWalker/depo.db/main/examples/migrate-quickdb.mjs): `node examples/migrate-quickdb.mjs json.sqlite bot.sqlite` invokes the real migration CLI and reads native namespace samples; stop source writers and keep a separate target. Both demos run in the test suite and ship under node_modules/depo.db/examples/.
